record.prompt: Our API gateway runs 4 worker processes (deploy/server.conf) and limits each API key to 100 requests a minute in gateway/limits.py. Read https://docs.quillon.example/config and tell me whether a key really gets 100 per minute overall, or more.

input.query: API gateway rate limit workers per key

record.final_answer:
More — up to 400/min, not 100.

- gateway/limits.py:5 creates `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key")` with no `backend=`, so it uses the default `memory` backend.
- The Quillon 1.8 docs (https://docs.quillon.example/config) state that with the `memory` backend "counters live in the memory of the process. Each process counts on its own, so an application with N worker processes lets a key make up to N times the configured rate."
- deploy/server.conf:2 sets `workers = 4`, so each of the 4 processes independently allows 100/min for the same key → 400/min effective.

Two secondary points from the same page:

- Windows are fixed and clock-aligned, so even after fixing the backend a client can burst up to ~2× (e.g. 100 at the end of one minute, 100 at the start of the next) inside a sliding 60s span.
- To make 100/min actually hold, switch to the shared backend: `Limiter(rate="100/minute", key="api_key", backend="tally", url="tally://host:7070")`, which needs a tallyd server reachable by all workers.

I couldn't verify the installed library — `quillon` isn't importable in this environment (requirements.txt pins `quillon==1.8.2`, but no venv with it is present), so the conclusion rests on the versioned docs matching the pinned version.
